title: The China Price
gist: Teaser of Zongyuan Zoe Liu's essay on Beijing's green path to ending dollar dominance; available text recounts the Bretton Woods and Connally history of U.S. currency power.

insights.claim: Beijing is described as pursuing a green path to ending dollar dominance, according to the essay's subtitle.
insights.speaker: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
insights.so_what: Links China's green-industrial push to de-dollarization; watch for energy-transition trade settled outside the dollar.

insights.claim: In 1971 Treasury Secretary John Connally told European finance ministers that the dollar was 'our currency, but your problem'.
insights.speaker: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
insights.so_what: Illustrates the asymmetry that motivates other states to seek alternatives to the dollar.

insights.claim: The dollar became the official reserve currency in 1944 under Bretton Woods, and even after the system collapsed and currencies floated, U.S. currency power expanded over the last half century as more countries integrated into the global economy.
insights.speaker: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
insights.so_what: Dollar dominance has been self-reinforcing with global integration, so displacing it is a multi-decade question.
insights.locator: The dollar had become that system's official reserve currency
